parts.latex: Hence, or otherwise, find the exact value of $\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\tan^2 x\left(\dfrac{\operatorname{cosec}x}{\operatorname{cosec}x-\sin x}\right)dx$

solutions.latex:
Writing $\operatorname{cosec}x=\dfrac{1}{\sin x}$ and multiplying numerator and denominator by $\sin x$:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{\operatorname{cosec}x}{\operatorname{cosec}x-\sin x}&=\dfrac{\frac{1}{\sin x}}{\frac{1}{\sin x}-\sin x}\\ &=\dfrac{1}{1-\sin^2 x}\\ &=\dfrac{1}{\cos^2 x} &&(\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1)\\ &=\sec^2 x \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the expression in terms of $\sin x$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using part (a), the integrand is $\tan^2 x\sec^2 x$, which has the form $f'(x)\big[f(x)\big]^2$ with $f(x)=\tan x$:
$$\begin{aligned} \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\tan^2 x\left(\dfrac{\operatorname{cosec}x}{\operatorname{cosec}x-\sin x}\right)dx&=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\tan^2 x\sec^2 x\,dx\\ &=\left[\dfrac{1}{3}\tan^3 x\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\\ &=\dfrac{1}{3}\left[\tan^3\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)-\tan^3(0)\right]\\ &=\dfrac{1}{3}\left[\left(\sqrt{3}\right)^3-0\right]\\ &=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(3\sqrt{3}\right)\\ &=\sqrt{3} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Recognises the integral is of the form $\displaystyle\int f'(x)\big[f(x)\big]^n\,dx$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using $1-\sin^2x=\cos^2x$:
$$\begin{aligned}\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\sqrt{\sin x-\sin^3x}\,dx&=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\sqrt{\sin x\left(1-\sin^2x\right)}\,dx\\&=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\sqrt{\sin x\cos^2x}\,dx\end{aligned}$$
Since $x\in\left[0,\,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, $\cos x\ge0$, so $\sqrt{\cos^2x}=\cos x$.
$$\begin{aligned}&=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\cos x(\sin x)^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dx\\&=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2}{3}\times\dfrac{3}{2}\cos x(\sin x)^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dx\\&=\dfrac{2}{3}\Big[(\sin x)^{\frac{3}{2}}\Big]_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\\&=\dfrac{2}{3}\left[\left(\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}-(\sin0)^{\frac{3}{2}}\right]\\&=\dfrac{2}{3}(1-0)\\&=\dfrac{2}{3}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct primitive $\dfrac{2}{3}(\sin x)^{\frac{3}{2}}$, or equivalent merit

Let $f(x)=\sin x$, so $f'(x)=\cos x$ and the integrand is $f'(x)[f(x)]^5$.

Using the reverse chain rule:
$$\int\cos x\sin^5x\,dx=\dfrac{1}{6}\sin^6x+c$$

$$\begin{aligned}\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^{\frac{3}{2}}+5x}}\,dx&=\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x\left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}+5\right)}}\,dx\\&=\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}\sqrt{x^{\frac{1}{2}}+5}}\,dx\\&=\int x^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}+5\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\,dx\end{aligned}$$
By the reverse chain rule, since $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}+5\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$:
$$\begin{aligned}\int x^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}+5\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\,dx&=2\int\dfrac{1}{2}x^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}+5\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\,dx\\&=4\left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}+5\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}+C\end{aligned}$$

The derivative of $4+3x^2$ is $6x$, so multiply and divide by $3$:
$$\begin{aligned} \int 2x(4+3x^2)^7\,dx&=\dfrac{1}{3}\int 6x(4+3x^2)^7\,dx \\ &=\dfrac{1}{3}\left[\dfrac{(4+3x^2)^8}{8}\right] \\ &=\dfrac{(4+3x^2)^8}{24}+C \end{aligned}$$
